\subsection{AdaptiveSpanAttention (\texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_adaptive_span_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Adaptive Span Attention (Sukhbaatar et al., 2019).  Mathematical Formulation:     1. Query-Key Attention Scores:        $$S\_{ij} = \frac{Q\_i K\_j^\top}{\sqrt{d}}$$          2. Dynamic Per-Head Span Masking:        Let $z\_h = \sigma(\text{logit}\_h) \cdot S\_{\max}$.        $$M\_{ij}^{(h)} = \begin{cases
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/adaptive\_span\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{AdaptiveSpanAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsection{TokenCompressedAttention (\texttt{token\_compressed})}
\label{sec:app_module_token_compressed}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Token-Compressed Attention Module. Compresses Key and Value sequence tokens using energy/norm selection while preserving [CLS] (index 0).
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/token\_compressed.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{token\_compressed} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TokenCompressedAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{token\_compressed} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{compression\_ratio}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{pretrained\_attn}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Massive Parameter Capacity}: Expands model expressivity across $E$ specialized experts with constant compute per token.
    \item \textbf{Dynamic Router Load Balancing}: Dispatches tokens adaptively using softmax routing with auxiliary entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{High-Efficiency Sparse Dispatch}: Executes parallel expert projections asynchronously across SM clusters.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Routing Communication Overhead}: All-to-all token dispatch across distributed nodes can introduce interconnect latency.
    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{token\_compressed} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsection{UnifiedRoPE (\texttt{unified\_rope})}
\label{sec:app_module_unified_rope}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Universal Rotary Position Embedding Attention module.  Subclasses :class:`BaseAttention` and applies rotary position embeddings to query and key representations prior to dot-product attention computation.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/unified\_rope.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{unified\_rope} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{UnifiedRoPE}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{unified\_rope} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{dim}: Hidden representation dimension.
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Number of attention heads.
    \item \texttt{max\_seq\_len}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{base}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.
    \item \textbf{Block-Sparse Memory Access}: Exploits structured sparsity patterns to reduce memory bandwidth roundtrips.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Irregular Memory Gather Overheads}: Fine-grained unstructured sparsity may incur GPU warp divergence.
    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{UPIMambaBlock (\texttt{upi\_stuffed\_mamba})}
\label{sec:app_module_upi_stuffed_mamba}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Bidirectional Uncertainty-Penalized Interpolated Mamba Block.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Given input sequence $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}$:     1. **Input Projections \& Symmetric Convolution:**        $$[X\_{\text{ssm}}, Z] = X W\_{\text{in}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times 2 D}$$
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/upi\_stuffed\_mamba.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{upi\_stuffed\_mamba} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{UPIMambaBlock}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{upi\_stuffed\_mamba} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.

    \item \texttt{dim}: Hidden representation dimension.

\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Recurrent State Horizon}: Very long associative horizons may require explicit decay gating to prevent historical interference.
    \item \textbf{Non-Causal Task Adaptation}: Requires bidirectional scan passes for non-causal masked language modeling tasks.
    \item \textbf{CUDA Kernel Specialization}: High performance requires customized fused scan Triton/CUDA implementations.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{ViGAttention (\texttt{vig\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_vig_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Vision GNN-inspired 2D Grid Linear Attention with Learned Gated Fusion.  Arranges the 1D sequence of length $N$ into a 2D spatial grid of dimensions $H\_g \times W\_g \approx \sqrt{N} \times \sqrt{N}$. Applies decoupled ELU kernel linear attention along rows ($H\_g$) and columns ($W\_g$), fusing the spa
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/vig\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{vig\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ViGAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{vig\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{xattention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}

\subsection{A3Compressor (\texttt{a3\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_a3_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
A3 Compressor: Activation-Aware SVD with Fisher weighting and LayerNorm recalibration.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/a3\_compressor.py}

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{a3\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}

\subsection{AASVDCompressor (\texttt{aa\_svd\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_aa_svd_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Activation-Aware SVD Compressor with streaming EMA covariance accumulation and true module replacement.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 4: Kernelized \& Spectral Attention
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/aa\_svd\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{aa\_svd\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{AASVDCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{aa\_svd\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\phi(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_1 x), \dots, \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_m x) \right]^\top, \\
M &= \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}, \quad Z = \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top \mathbf{1} \in \mathbb{R}^m, \\
O_t &= \frac{\phi(Q_t) M_t}{\phi(Q_t) Z_t + \epsilon}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}

\begin{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Linear Autoregressive Inference}: Re-orders computation via associativity $\phi(Q) (\phi(K)^\top V)$ for $\mathcal{O}(1)$ step decoding.
    \item \textbf{Frequency-Domain Spectral Mixing}: Projects token sequences into Fourier frequency spaces for global mixing.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Feature Map Variance}: Small feature dimension $m$ can exhibit higher approximation variance on sharp attention distributions.
    \item \textbf{Normalization Instability}: Requires small $\epsilon$ stabilization in the denominator $(\phi(Q) \sum \phi(K)^\top + \epsilon)^{-1}$.
    \item \textbf{Orthogonal Resampling Overhead}: Periodic resampling of projection matrices $\omega$ is required during long training.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Aasvd (\texttt{aasvd})}
\label{sec:app_module_aasvd}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{aasvd} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/aasvd.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{aasvd} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Aasvd}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{aasvd} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{aasvd} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{admm\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{sparsity}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{quant\_bits}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rho1}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rho2}: Operational hyperparameter.

\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Massive Parameter Capacity}: Expands model expressivity across $E$ specialized experts with constant compute per token.
    \item \textbf{Dynamic Router Load Balancing}: Dispatches tokens adaptively using softmax routing with auxiliary entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{High-Efficiency Sparse Dispatch}: Executes parallel expert projections asynchronously across SM clusters.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Routing Communication Overhead}: All-to-all token dispatch across distributed nodes can introduce interconnect latency.
    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{ADMMMaskedLinear (\texttt{admm\_pruner})}
\label{sec:app_module_admm_pruner}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Linear layer maintaining continuous weights and an ADMM-derived binary mask with STE gradient backprop.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/admm\_pruner.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{admm\_pruner} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ADMMMaskedLinear}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{admm\_pruner} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{ASTPruner (\texttt{ast\_pruner})}
\label{sec:app_module_ast_pruner}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
AST Pruner: Vectorized semi-structured 2:4 and N:M pruning engine with empirical Fisher calibration and PCA coordinate rotation.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/ast\_pruner.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{ast\_pruner} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ASTPruner}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{ast\_pruner} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{bonsai\_pruner} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
CR (Column-Row / Interpolative Decomposition) Compressor. Decomposes linear layers into skeleton column bases and interpolative projections.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     rank: Rank parameter (number of skeleton columns).     cfg: Optional configuration object.     target\_layers: Optional tar
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/cr\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{cr\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{CRCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{cr\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{in\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{out\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{bias}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{dtype}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{device}: Operational hyperparameter.

\subsection{CURCompressor (\texttt{cur\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_cur_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Compressor that replaces eligible Linear layers with CURLinear.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/cur\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{cur\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{CURCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{cur\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{method}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{cfg}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{target\_names}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{deterministic}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{CURMoECompressor (\texttt{cur\_moe\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_cur_moe_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Compresses Mixture of Experts (MoE) layers using CUR cross-approximation.  Args:     model: PyTorch model containing MoE modules.     rank: Target rank for CUR decomposition of expert weights.     method: 'leverage' (statistical leverage scores) or 'energy' (Frobenius energy).     cfg: Optional conf
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/cur\_moe\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{cur\_moe\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{CURMoECompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{cur\_moe\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
DeltaKV Compressor: Decomposes projection weights into a low-rank reference component plus sparse residuals, modeling weight matrices under residual delta formulation.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     rank: Rank of reference low-rank matrix (default 16).     sparsity: Fraction of sparse residual
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/delta\_kv.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{delta\_kv} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{DeltaKVCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{delta\_kv} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{max\_refs}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{topk}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{compression\_ratio}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{residual\_threshold}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{DirectSVDCompressor (\texttt{direct\_svd})}
\label{sec:app_module_direct_svd}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Direct SVD Compressor.  Performs direct truncated SVD on all linear layers:     W $\approx$ U\_r * Sigma\_r * V\_r^T Allocates singular energy symmetrically:     U\_factor = U\_r * sqrt(Sigma\_r)     V\_factor = sqrt(Sigma\_r) * V\_r^T and replaces dense nn.Linear layers with factorized SVDLinear modules to achieve
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/direct\_svd.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{direct\_svd} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{DirectSVDCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{direct\_svd} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{min\_rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{rank\_ratio}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{target\_modules}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{DynamicEntropySVDCompressorRegistered (\texttt{dynamic\_rank})}
\label{sec:app_module_dynamic_rank}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Dynamic Entropy SVD Compressor.  1. Computes singular entropy H(Sigma\_l) on layer activation covariances or weights. 2. Allocates layer ranks within [min\_rank, max\_rank] subject to parameter/rank budget. 3. Replaces nn.Linear layers with DynamicSVDLinear factorized modules.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/dynamic\_rank.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{dynamic\_rank} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{DynamicEntropySVDCompressorRegistered}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{dynamic\_rank} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{EntropyBudgetCompressor (\texttt{entropy\_budget\_allocation})}
\label{sec:app_module_entropy_budget_allocation}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Entropy Budget Low-Rank SVD Compressor.  Computes activation covariance and whiten weights, calculates per-component singular entropy contributions, allocates low-rank budgets globally across layers, and replaces dense nn.Linear layers with factorized SVDLinear modules with symmetric singular value
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/entropy\_budget\_allocation.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{entropy\_budget\_allocation} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{EntropyBudgetCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{entropy\_budget\_allocation} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{ERCCompressor (\texttt{erc\_svd})}
\label{sec:app_module_erc_svd}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Error-Controlled SVD (ERC-SVD) Compressor.  Finds the minimal rank r for each linear layer such that the relative Frobenius reconstruction error ||W - W\_r||\_F / ||W||\_F is guaranteed to be <= allowed\_error (i.e. singular energy retention sum\_{i=1}^r sigma\_i^2 / sum\_j sigma\_j^2 >= 1 - allowed\_error^2
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/erc\_svd.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{erc\_svd} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ERCCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{erc\_svd} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{allowed\_error}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{target\_modules}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{FAQQuantizer (\texttt{faq\_quantizer})}
\label{sec:app_module_faq_quantizer}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
FAQQuantizer: Feature-Activation-Aware Quantization. Collects activation statistics to scale channel-wise quantization step sizes, minimizing activation-weighted reconstruction distortion.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     tokenizer: Optional tokenizer for text-based calibration.     bits: Quanti
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/faq\_quantizer.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{faq\_quantizer} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FAQQuantizer}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{faq\_quantizer} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{FLAPCompressor (\texttt{flap})}
\label{sec:app_module_flap}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
FLAP Compressor: Fluctuation-based Adaptive Structured Pruning.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/flap.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{flap} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FLAPCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{flap} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}

    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$

\subsection{Frandi (\texttt{frandi})}
\label{sec:app_module_frandi}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{frandi} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/frandi.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{frandi} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Frandi}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{frandi} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{frandi} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \label{sec:app_module_frandi_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
FRanDI (Feature-Regression aligned SVD) Compressor. Compresses linear layers using singular value decomposition with optional activation alignment and adaptive energy-preservation thresholding.  Args:     model: Model to compress.     rank: Target rank when energy\_threshold is None.     energy\_thres
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/frandi\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{frandi\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FRanDICompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{frandi\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{GFWSCompressor (\texttt{gfws\_d\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_gfws_d_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Generalized Fisher / Covariance-Weighted SVD Compressor. Whitens weights using empirical input activation covariance square-root Cov(X)^{1/2}, performs low-rank truncated SVD, and de-whitens to restore optimal compressed weights.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/gfws\_d\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{gfws\_d\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{GFWSCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{gfws\_d\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{HashedLinear (\texttt{hashed\_linear})}
\label{sec:app_module_hashed_linear}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Linear layer with weight sharing via a compact parameter hash table. W\_{i, j} = xi(i, j) * w[h(i, j)]
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/hashed\_linear.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{hashed\_linear} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{HashedLinear}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{hashed\_linear} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{in\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{out\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{n\_buckets}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{bias}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{use\_sign}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{dtype}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{HashedNetCompressor (\texttt{hashed\_net\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_hashed_net_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Compress a model by replacing every nn.Linear layer with HashedLinear, which shares weights globally through compact hash tables.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     rank: Rank parameter (optionally maps to bucket budget).     n\_buckets: Number of hash buckets (size of shared weight table).     use
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/hashed\_net\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{hashed\_net\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{HashedNetCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{hashed\_net\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{n\_buckets}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{use\_sign}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{cfg}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{target\_layers}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Hybrid SVD Compressor.  Replaces transformer multi-head self-attention mechanisms with SVDSingleHead spectral projection modules and DirectSVDEncoderLayer blocks.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     svd\_rank: SVD rank for single-head projection.     rank: Optional alias for svd\_rank.     target\_mod

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{hybrid\_svd\_layer} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}

\subsection{Hybridkv (\texttt{hybridkv})}
\label{sec:app_module_hybridkv}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{hybridkv} operator implements an optimized track 5: quantization \& compression engines within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Quantization \& Compression Engines
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/hybridkv.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{hybridkv} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Hybridkv}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{hybridkv} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
s &= \frac{\max(W) - \min(W)}{2^b - 1}, \quad z = \operatorname{round}\left(-\frac{\min(W)}{s}\right), \\
Q &= \operatorname{clip}\left(\operatorname{round}\left(\frac{W}{s}\right) + z, 0, 2^b - 1\right), \\
\hat{W} &= s \cdot (Q - z) \approx W.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d / \gamma)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \cdot b)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Reduces memory traffic by $4\times$ to $8\times$ with sub-byte integer representation, accelerating memory-bound decoding.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Activation Outlier Channel Isolation}: Retains salient $1\%$ activation outlier channels in FP16 to prevent quantization collapse.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Weighted Error Minimization}: Solves optimal rounding $\min \|(W - \hat{W}) H\|_F^2$ to minimize downstream perplexity degradation.
    \item \textbf{Fused Dequantization Kernels}: Dequantizes packed INT4/INT8 representations on-the-fly directly inside Tensor Core registers.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Calibration Dataset Dependence}: Outlier detection and Hessian estimation require representative calibration batches.
    \item \textbf{Mixed-Precision Arithmetic Complexity}: Packing sub-byte integers requires specialized bit-shift instructions.
    \item \textbf{Non-Uniform Codebook Latency}: Highly non-linear codebooks require lookup table lookups on edge devices.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
HybridKV Compressor: Classifies attention projection heads into static/dynamic types and configures hierarchical dynamic KV cache budgets without altering model stationary weights.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     budget: Overall fraction of KV cache budget to retain (default 0.3).     static\_ra
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/hybridkv\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{hybridkv\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{HybridKVCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{hybridkv\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{KMeansCompressor (\texttt{kmeans\_quantize})}
\label{sec:app_module_kmeans_quantize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
KMeansCompressor: Vector quantization via scalar k-means clustering of weight parameters.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     n\_clusters: Number of centroid codebook entries (default 256 -> 8 bits, 16 -> 4 bits).     bits: Optional bitwidth constraint (e.g. 4 or 8) which sets n\_clusters = 2**bits.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Quantization \& Compression Engines
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/kmeans\_quantize.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{kmeans\_quantize} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{KMeansCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{kmeans\_quantize} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
s &= \frac{\max(W) - \min(W)}{2^b - 1}, \quad z = \operatorname{round}\left(-\frac{\min(W)}{s}\right), \\
Q &= \operatorname{clip}\left(\operatorname{round}\left(\frac{W}{s}\right) + z, 0, 2^b - 1\right), \\
\hat{W} &= s \cdot (Q - z) \approx W.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d / \gamma)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \cdot b)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Reduces memory traffic by $4\times$ to $8\times$ with sub-byte integer representation, accelerating memory-bound decoding.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{linear}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{n\_clusters}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{bits}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{KroneckerCompressor (\texttt{kronecker\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_kronecker_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Compresses a model by replacing every eligible nn.Linear layer with a Kronecker product decomposition (A $\otimes$ B), falling back to low-rank SVD when dimensions do not allow composite factorization.  Args:     model: PyTorch model to compress (optional if instantiated as standalone engine).     rank: Ran
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/kronecker\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{kronecker\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{KroneckerCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{kronecker\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{cfg}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{target\_layers}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\label{sec:app_module_kronecker_linear}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Linear layer whose weight matrix is parameterised as the Kronecker product of two smaller factor matrices: W = A $\otimes$ B.  For W in R^{out\_features x in\_features}, with out\_features = m1 * m2 and in\_features = n1 * n2: - A in R^{m1 x n1} - B in R^{m2 x n2}  Forward contraction uses the vectorization ide
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/kronecker\_linear.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{kronecker\_linear} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{KroneckerLinear}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{kronecker\_linear} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}

\subsection{Kvtc (\texttt{kvtc})}
\label{sec:app_module_kvtc}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{kvtc} operator implements an optimized track 5: quantization \& compression engines within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Quantization \& Compression Engines
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/kvtc.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{kvtc} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Kvtc}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{kvtc} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
s &= \frac{\max(W) - \min(W)}{2^b - 1}, \quad z = \operatorname{round}\left(-\frac{\min(W)}{s}\right), \\
Q &= \operatorname{clip}\left(\operatorname{round}\left(\frac{W}{s}\right) + z, 0, 2^b - 1\right), \\
\hat{W} &= s \cdot (Q - z) \approx W.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d / \gamma)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \cdot b)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Reduces memory traffic by $4\times$ to $8\times$ with sub-byte integer representation, accelerating memory-bound decoding.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Activation Outlier Channel Isolation}: Retains salient $1\%$ activation outlier channels in FP16 to prevent quantization collapse.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Weighted Error Minimization}: Solves optimal rounding $\min \|(W - \hat{W}) H\|_F^2$ to minimize downstream perplexity degradation.
    \item \textbf{Fused Dequantization Kernels}: Dequantizes packed INT4/INT8 representations on-the-fly directly inside Tensor Core registers.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Calibration Dataset Dependence}: Outlier detection and Hessian estimation require representative calibration batches.
    \item \textbf{Mixed-Precision Arithmetic Complexity}: Packing sub-byte integers requires specialized bit-shift instructions.
    \item \textbf{Non-Uniform Codebook Latency}: Highly non-linear codebooks require lookup table lookups on edge devices.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{KVTCCompressor (\texttt{kvtc\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_kvtc_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
KVTC: KV Cache Transform Coding compressor. Compresses linear projection weights using PCA decorrelation, adaptive quantization, and entropy coding estimation.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     bits: Quantization bit-width (default 4).     pca\_energy: Fraction of PCA energy retained (default 0.95
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/kvtc\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{kvtc\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{KVTCCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{kvtc\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{bits}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{pca\_energy}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{LIFTRCompressor (\texttt{liftr})}
\label{sec:app_module_liftr}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
LIFTR Compressor: Linearizes activations and attention mechanisms for ultra-low latency.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/liftr.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{liftr} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{LIFTRCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{liftr} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{High-Efficiency Sparse Dispatch}: Executes parallel expert projections asynchronously across SM clusters.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Routing Communication Overhead}: All-to-all token dispatch across distributed nodes can introduce interconnect latency.
    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{mamba\_shedder} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}
