\subsection{MGIECompressor (\texttt{mgie\_svd})}
\label{sec:app_module_mgie_svd}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
MGIE-SVD Compressor (Maximum Information Entropy SVD).  Analyzes each weight matrix's singular spectrum, computes normalized Shannon singular entropy:     p\_i = sigma\_i**2 / sum\_j(sigma\_j**2)     H = -sum\_i(p\_i * ln(p\_i)) dynamically determines optimal truncation rank r\_l proportional to H, factoriz
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/mgie\_svd.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{mgie\_svd} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{MGIECompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{mgie\_svd} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\label{sec:app_module_mgie_svd_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
MGIE-SVD Budget Compressor: Global Entropy-Proportional Rank Allocation.  Calculates Shannon singular entropy for all linear layers across the network, distributes a global total rank budget proportionally according to spectral information density, factorizes weights using symmetric square-root sing
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 4: Kernelized \& Spectral Attention
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/mgie\_svd\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{mgie\_svd\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{MGIESVDBudgetCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{mgie\_svd\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\phi(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_1 x), \dots, \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_m x) \right]^\top, \\
M &= \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}, \quad Z = \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top \mathbf{1} \in \mathbb{R}^m, \\
O_t &= \frac{\phi(Q_t) M_t}{\phi(Q_t) Z_t + \epsilon}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly linear in $N$ via positive feature mapping $\phi(x)$, enabling streaming $O(1)$ state updates.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Positive Orthogonal Random Features (FAVOR+)}: Provides unbiased estimation of softmax attention without negative values.
    \item \textbf{Linear Autoregressive Inference}: Re-orders computation via associativity $\phi(Q) (\phi(K)^\top V)$ for $\mathcal{O}(1)$ step decoding.
    \item \textbf{Frequency-Domain Spectral Mixing}: Projects token sequences into Fourier frequency spaces for global mixing.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Feature Map Variance}: Small feature dimension $m$ can exhibit higher approximation variance on sharp attention distributions.
    \item \textbf{Normalization Instability}: Requires small $\epsilon$ stabilization in the denominator $(\phi(Q) \sum \phi(K)^\top + \epsilon)^{-1}$.
    \item \textbf{Orthogonal Resampling Overhead}: Periodic resampling of projection matrices $\omega$ is required during long training.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{MoDeGPTCompressor (\texttt{modegpt\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_modegpt_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
MoDeGPT: Modular Decomposition of Transformer Projection Blocks. Decomposes paired linear projections (e.g. Q \& K, Gate \& Up, or consecutive linear layers) jointly into shared low-rank subspaces:     [W\_1; W\_2] = U\_r S\_r V\_r^T + E  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     rank: Rank for low-rank joint de
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/modegpt\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{modegpt\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{MoDeGPTCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{modegpt\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.

\subsection{NLISoftmaxCompressor (\texttt{nli\_softmax})}
\label{sec:app_module_nli_softmax}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Compressor that replaces standard softmax layers with quantization-friendly NLI softmax.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Quantization \& Compression Engines
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/nli\_softmax.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{nli\_softmax} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{NLISoftmaxCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{nli\_softmax} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
s &= \frac{\max(W) - \min(W)}{2^b - 1}, \quad z = \operatorname{round}\left(-\frac{\min(W)}{s}\right), \\
Q &= \operatorname{clip}\left(\operatorname{round}\left(\frac{W}{s}\right) + z, 0, 2^b - 1\right), \\
\hat{W} &= s \cdot (Q - z) \approx W.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d / \gamma)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \cdot b)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Reduces memory traffic by $4\times$ to $8\times$ with sub-byte integer representation, accelerating memory-bound decoding.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Hessian-Weighted Error Minimization}: Solves optimal rounding $\min \|(W - \hat{W}) H\|_F^2$ to minimize downstream perplexity degradation.
    \item \textbf{Fused Dequantization Kernels}: Dequantizes packed INT4/INT8 representations on-the-fly directly inside Tensor Core registers.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Calibration Dataset Dependence}: Outlier detection and Hessian estimation require representative calibration batches.
    \item \textbf{Mixed-Precision Arithmetic Complexity}: Packing sub-byte integers requires specialized bit-shift instructions.
    \item \textbf{Non-Uniform Codebook Latency}: Highly non-linear codebooks require lookup table lookups on edge devices.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{NMFCompressor (\texttt{nmf\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_nmf_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) Compressor. Decomposes linear layer weights into low-rank non-negative factors.  Args:     model: Model to compress.     rank: Target rank for NMF factorization.     max\_iter: Maximum multiplicative update iterations.     cfg: Optional configuration object.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/nmf\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{nmf\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{NMFCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{nmf\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Oats (\texttt{oats})}
\label{sec:app_module_oats}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{oats} operator implements an optimized track 3: mixture-of-experts \& dynamic routing within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/oats.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{oats} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Oats}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{oats} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).

    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{OptimalSubspaceProjectionCompressor (\texttt{optimal\_subspace\_projection})}
\label{sec:app_module_optimal_subspace_projection}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Optimal Subspace Projection Compressor using activation-aware randomized SVD.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/optimal\_subspace\_projection.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{optimal\_subspace\_projection} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{OptimalSubspaceProjectionCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{optimal\_subspace\_projection} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{PADReAttention (\texttt{padre\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_padre_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Polynomial Attention with Dropout Regularization (PADRe).  Args:     config: model configuration (HuggingFace style)     order: degree of the polynomial kernel (higher = closer to softmax)     temperature: scaling factor applied before polynomial
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/padre\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{padre\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{PADReAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{padre\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{order}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{temperature}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Context}: Retains dense local syntactic interactions while routing global anchor tokens.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.
    \item \textbf{Block-Sparse Memory Access}: Exploits structured sparsity patterns to reduce memory bandwidth roundtrips.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Irregular Memory Gather Overheads}: Fine-grained unstructured sparsity may incur GPU warp divergence.
    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{ResSVDCompressorRegistered (\texttt{res\_svd})}
\label{sec:app_module_res_svd}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Spectral Residual LoRA (Res-SVD) Compressor.  Replaces standard Linear layers with ResSVDLinear modules, truncating base weights at rank r (frozen) and initializing adapter matrices A, B directly from the residual error tail.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/res\_svd.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{res\_svd} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ResSVDCompressorRegistered}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{res\_svd} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{in\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{out\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{base\_rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{residual\_rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{scaling}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{factorize\_base}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{RotationalSliceGPTINT4Compressor (\texttt{rotational\_slicegpt\_int4})}
\label{sec:app_module_rotational_slicegpt_int4}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Rotational-SliceGPT-INT4 Hybrid Compression Engine. Combines orthogonal rotation, variance-based coordinate slicing, and second-order Hessian INT4 non-uniform quantization.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/rotational\_slicegpt\_int4.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{rotational\_slicegpt\_int4} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{RotationalSliceGPTINT4Compressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{rotational\_slicegpt\_int4} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{RPCAttention (\texttt{rpc\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_rpc_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{rpc\\_attention} operator implements an optimized track 5: structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/rpc\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{rpc\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{RPCAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{rpc\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}

\subsection{Rpca (\texttt{rpca})}
\label{sec:app_module_rpca}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{rpca} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/rpca.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{rpca} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Rpca}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{rpca} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{rpca} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsection{RPCACompressor (\texttt{rpca\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_rpca_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA) Low-Rank Compressor.  Decomposes weight matrices W into low-rank component L and sparse outlier matrix S via Principal Component Pursuit / alternating soft-thresholding:     min ||L||\_* + lambda ||S||\_1  s.t.  W = L + S Factorizes the low-rank component L i
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/rpca\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{rpca\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{RPCACompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{rpca\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.

\subsection{SaesSvd (\texttt{saes\_svd})}
\label{sec:app_module_saes_svd}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{saes\\_svd} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/saes\_svd.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{saes\_svd} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SaesSvd}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{saes\_svd} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Context}: Retains dense local syntactic interactions while routing global anchor tokens.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.
    \item \textbf{Block-Sparse Memory Access}: Exploits structured sparsity patterns to reduce memory bandwidth roundtrips.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Irregular Memory Gather Overheads}: Fine-grained unstructured sparsity may incur GPU warp divergence.
    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{salr} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsection{Sdrm (\texttt{sdrm})}
\label{sec:app_module_sdrm}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{sdrm} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/sdrm.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{sdrm} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Sdrm}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{sdrm} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

Table~\ref{tab:telemetry_sdrm} reports the empirical hardware performance measurements recorded on an isolated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (8GB VRAM, CUDA 12.4, AMP FP16 enabled, batch size $B=4$, sequence length $L=128$).

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{sdrm} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsection{SliceGPTCompressor (\texttt{slicegpt})}
\label{sec:app_module_slicegpt}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Native PyTorch SliceGPT Compressor.  Applies orthogonal transformation Q to rotate model representations onto principal activation variance coordinates, followed by uniform or non-uniform projection head slicing.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/slicegpt.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{slicegpt} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SliceGPTCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{slicegpt} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{tokenizer}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{sparsity}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{non\_uniform}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{calibration\_loader}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{calibration\_texts}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Dynamic Router Load Balancing}: Dispatches tokens adaptively using softmax routing with auxiliary entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{High-Efficiency Sparse Dispatch}: Executes parallel expert projections asynchronously across SM clusters.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Routing Communication Overhead}: All-to-all token dispatch across distributed nodes can introduce interconnect latency.
    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\label{sec:app_module_slim_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
SLiM Compressor: One-shot joint b-bit quantization, 2:4 structured sparsity, and low-rank residual recovery.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/slim\_compressor.py}

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{slim\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}

\subsection{Soka (\texttt{soka})}
\label{sec:app_module_soka}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{soka} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/soka.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{soka} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Soka}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{soka} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{soka} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsection{SpectraformerAttention (\texttt{spectraformer\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_spectraformer_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{spectraformer\\_attention} operator implements an optimized track 5: structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/spectraformer\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{spectraformer\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SpectraformerAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{spectraformer\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{SubspaceProjectionCompressor (\texttt{subspace\_projection})}
\label{sec:app_module_subspace_projection}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Subspace Projection Compression Engine. Compresses neural networks by projecting weight matrices onto their principal subspaces, replacing dense linear layers with factorized SubspaceLinear modules.  Args:     model: PyTorch model to compress.     rank: Subspace rank.     method: Subspace decomposit
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/subspace\_projection.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{subspace\_projection} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SubspaceProjectionCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{subspace\_projection} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

    \item \texttt{in\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.

\subsection{SVDLinearCompressor (\texttt{svd\_linear})}
\label{sec:app_module_svd_linear}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Compresses model by replacing Linear layers with SVDLinearLayer.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 4: Kernelized \& Spectral Attention
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/svd\_linear.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{svd\_linear} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SVDLinearCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{svd\_linear} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\phi(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_1 x), \dots, \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_m x) \right]^\top, \\
M &= \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}, \quad Z = \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top \mathbf{1} \in \mathbb{R}^m, \\
O_t &= \frac{\phi(Q_t) M_t}{\phi(Q_t) Z_t + \epsilon}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly linear in $N$ via positive feature mapping $\phi(x)$, enabling streaming $O(1)$ state updates.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{linear\_layer}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{use\_fused\_kernel}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{use\_rms\_norm}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{eps}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Positive Orthogonal Random Features (FAVOR+)}: Provides unbiased estimation of softmax attention without negative values.
    \item \textbf{Linear Autoregressive Inference}: Re-orders computation via associativity $\phi(Q) (\phi(K)^\top V)$ for $\mathcal{O}(1)$ step decoding.
    \item \textbf{Frequency-Domain Spectral Mixing}: Projects token sequences into Fourier frequency spaces for global mixing.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Feature Map Variance}: Small feature dimension $m$ can exhibit higher approximation variance on sharp attention distributions.
    \item \textbf{Normalization Instability}: Requires small $\epsilon$ stabilization in the denominator $(\phi(Q) \sum \phi(K)^\top + \epsilon)^{-1}$.
    \item \textbf{Orthogonal Resampling Overhead}: Periodic resampling of projection matrices $\omega$ is required during long training.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{SwiftSVDCompressor (\texttt{swift\_svd})}
\label{sec:app_module_swift_svd}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Swift-SVD Compressor: Fast Closed-Form Truncated SVD.  Decomposes dense weight matrices into rank-r factorized layers with symmetric square-root singular value splitting (U\_r * sqrt(Sigma\_r), sqrt(Sigma\_r) * V\_r^T) and replaces nn.Linear with factorized SVDLinear modules.  Args:     model: Model to
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/swift\_svd.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{swift\_svd} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SwiftSVDCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{swift\_svd} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{rank\_ratio}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{target\_modules}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{swift\_svd\_compressor} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsection{TLinFormerAttention (\texttt{tlinformer\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_tlinformer_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{tlinformer\\_attention} operator implements an optimized track 5: structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/tlinformer\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{tlinformer\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TLinFormerAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{tlinformer\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{ToMoECompressor (\texttt{tomoe\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_tomoe_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Converts FFN layers into Mixture of Experts via weight clustering.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     num\_experts: number of experts per MoE layer (default 4).     top\_k: number of active experts per token (default 2).
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/tomoe\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{tomoe\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ToMoECompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{tomoe\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{original}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{num\_experts}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{top\_k}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{TTCompressor (\texttt{tt\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_tt_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Compressor that replaces nn.Linear layers with Tensor-Train (TTLinearLayer) modules.  Args:     model: PyTorch model to compress.     rank: Rank parameter (alias for tt\_rank).     tt\_rank: TT-rank bound for tensor-train cores.     cfg: Optional configuration object.     target\_layers: Optional list
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/tt\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{tt\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TTCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{tt\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{tt\_rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.

\end{itemize}

\subsection{TTLinearLayer (\texttt{tt\_linear})}
\label{sec:app_module_tt_linear}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Tensor-Train (TT) Linear Layer. Represents weight matrix W in R^{out\_features x in\_features} as a sequence of d TT-cores: G\_1, G\_2, ..., G\_d where core G\_k has shape (r\_{k-1}, p\_k, q\_k, r\_k) with boundary ranks r\_0 = r\_d = 1.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/tt\_linear.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{tt\_linear} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TTLinearLayer}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{tt\_linear} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{in\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{out\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{tt\_rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{bias}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{shape}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{dtype}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{uniql\_compressor} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsection{ZerokvNeo (\texttt{zerokv\_neo})}
\label{sec:app_module_zerokv_neo}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{zerokv\\_neo} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/zerokv\_neo.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{zerokv\_neo} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ZerokvNeo}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{zerokv\_neo} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\label{sec:app_module_zerokv_neo_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
ZeroKV-Neo Compressor: L2-norm weight pruning preserving attention sinks and heavy hitters.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     keep\_ratio: Fraction of output neurons to retain (default 0.3).     num\_attention\_sinks: Number of initial sink channels pinned (default 4).     heavy\_hitter\_ratio: Fracti
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/compression\_engine/zerokv\_neo\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{zerokv\_neo\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ZeroKVNeoCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{zerokv\_neo\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Massive Parameter Capacity}: Expands model expressivity across $E$ specialized experts with constant compute per token.
    \item \textbf{Dynamic Router Load Balancing}: Dispatches tokens adaptively using softmax routing with auxiliary entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{High-Efficiency Sparse Dispatch}: Executes parallel expert projections asynchronously across SM clusters.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Routing Communication Overhead}: All-to-all token dispatch across distributed nodes can introduce interconnect latency.
    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}
